anomaly_def.Name: Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Critical engine-level settings (memory pools, checkpoint cadence, parallelism, etc.) are mis-tuned relative to hardware capacity and workload demands, so the problem originates from the parameter choices themselves rather than from true resource scarcity.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : Sessions repeatedly serialize on buffer-cache pages, latches, or page-pin structures, causing buffer-busy waits, CPU spin, and I/O stalls even when aggregate resources appear sufficient.

When both root causes are present, the system simultaneously suffers from mis-sized or overly aggressive configuration parameters and from intensified contention inside the buffer manager. Observable symptoms blend and amplify:  
• Extreme and oscillating buffer-busy/latch wait counts alongside spikes of log-write, checkpoint, or background-writer waits that do not correlate with actual hardware usage.  
• CPU cores alternate between idle periods (due to throttling by mis-tuned parameters) and 100 % spin-loops (due to latch storms).  
• Sudden latency cliff after configuration changes or upgrades, followed by cascading stalls in buffer I/O, prolonged checkpoint completion, and lock escalations at higher tiers.  
• Monitoring tools may falsely suggest memory pressure, yet page-in/out rates stay high because the undersized buffer pool forces constant eviction, further aggravating hot-page contention.  

Causal chain: misconfigured parameters—such as a too-small buffer pool, overly frequent checkpoints, or an excessive max_parallelism value—create rapid page churn and frequent dirty-page flushing. This churn elevates demand on shared hotspot pages and on the buffer manager’s latch structures. The heightened contention lengthens critical sections, causing spin-loops that waste CPU cycles and delay I/O completion. The resulting throughput collapse, in turn, leads administrators to raise connection or parallel-worker limits, which further magnifies both latch pressure and configuration misfit. Thus, the two anomalies reinforce each other: poor configuration provokes buffer-level thrashing, and the ensuing latch contention obscures the original tuning fault, jointly degrading performance far more than either issue alone.

entry.official_description: This member joined a group on which all members do not support member actions, as such it did reset its member configuration to the default one.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
